# SEC TRIBUNAL — PROSECUTION'S BEAR CASE
## In re: Apple Inc. (AAPL, CIK 0000320193)

Your Honors, the defense will parade headline growth before this Tribunal. The Prosecution asks the court to look beneath it. The record — Apple's own sworn filings — reveals stagnation, cash-flow erosion, and a recent sequential deterioration the defense would prefer you not examine.

---

**CHARGE 1: A Multi-Year Growth Stall — Three Fiscal Years of Near-Zero Progress.**
Between FY2022 and FY2024, revenue went essentially nowhere: $394.33B (FY2022), then an outright **contraction of -2.8% to $383.29B in FY2023**, followed by a feeble +2.0% recovery to $391.04B in FY2024 — still *below* the FY2022 level two full years later [Exhibit A]. A company priced for growth that cannot exceed its own two-year-old revenue figure has, on the evidence, stalled.

**CHARGE 2: Net Income Declined Two Consecutive Fiscal Years.**
Net income fell from $99.80B (FY2022) to $97.00B (FY2023) to **$93.74B (FY2024)** — a cumulative decline of over $6B across two years, with net margin compressing from 25.3% to **24.0%** in FY2024 [Exhibit A]. The bottom line shrank even as the topline treaded water.

**CHARGE 3: Operating Cash Flow Is Erratic and Declining at the Peak.**
Operating cash flow peaked at $122.15B in FY2022, collapsed to $110.54B in FY2023, and — most damning — **fell again in FY2025 to $111.48B from $118.25B in FY2024**, a ~$6.8B decline in the very year the defense claims record strength [Exhibit A]. Reported earnings rose in FY2025; cash generation fell. The court should ask why the cash does not follow the accounting.

**CHARGE 4: Alarming Sequential Deterioration in the Most Recent Quarters.**
The latest three reported quarters show a steep slide: revenue of $143.76B (Q ending 2025-12-27) fell to $111.18B (2026-03-28) and again to **$109.42B (2026-06-27)** [Exhibit A]. Operating income cratered from $50.85B to $35.88B to $35.70B over the same span — a **~30% sequential collapse** — with operating margin dropping from 35.4% to 32.6% [Exhibit A]. Gross profit was flat quarter-over-quarter ($54.78B vs. $54.77B) while cash & equivalents drained from $45.57B to **$39.54B** in a single quarter [Exhibit A]. The most recent evidence in the record points downward.

**CHARGE 5: A Balance Sheet Historically Hollowed Out by Leverage.**
At FY2022, stockholders' equity had been ground down to a mere **$50.67B against $302.08B in total liabilities** — liabilities nearly six times equity — with LT-debt/equity at **1.95** [Exhibit A]. Cash & equivalents were simultaneously depleted from $38.02B (FY2020) to **$23.65B (FY2022)** [Exhibit A]. Total liabilities then *rose again* to **$308.03B in FY2024**, up from $290.44B in FY2023 [Exhibit A]. This is a company that spent years running its equity cushion to the bone.

**CHARGE 6: Rising Cost of Capital and Ballooning R&D With Diminishing Returns.**
Interest expense climbed from $2.65B (FY2021) to **$3.93B (FY2023)** — a 48% increase in two years [Exhibit A]. Meanwhile, R&D spend surged 58% from $21.91B (FY2021) to $34.55B (FY2025), and hit **$11.73B in the single quarter ending 2026-06-27** — even as that quarter's revenue *declined sequentially* [Exhibit A]. The company is paying more to borrow and spending more to innovate, while its most recent quarters shrink.

---

**PROSECUTION'S SUMMATION:** The filings show a company that stalled for three fiscal years, saw net income fall twice, generated *less* operating cash in FY2025 than in FY2024, and — in the freshest quarters before this court — posted sequential declines in revenue, operating income, and cash. The Prosecution rests.
defense:
# SEC TRIBUNAL — DEFENSE REBUTTAL
## In re: Apple Inc. (AAPL, CIK 0000320193)

Your Honors, the Prosecution has built its case on stale fiscal years and a misreading of seasonality. The freshest evidence in the record — the quarters ending December 2025 through June 2026 — shows record margins, double-digit growth, a rebuilt balance sheet, and surging cash generation. The Defense answers each charge in turn.

---

**REBUTTAL TO CHARGE 1: The "Growth Stall" Ended — Decisively — Before This Trial Began.**

The Prosecution's case ends conveniently at FY2024. The record does not. FY2025 revenue was **$416.16B, up 6.4%** and well above the FY2022 "ceiling" of $394.33B [Exhibit A]. The two most recent quarters show revenue growth of **+16.6% and +16.4% year-over-year** [Exhibit A] — squarely in line with the sector: Microsoft's comparable quarters grew 16.7% and 18.3% [Exhibit B].

An honest concession: during FY2023–2024, Apple did underperform its peer — Microsoft grew 26.1% in FY2023 while Apple contracted 2.8% [Exhibits A, B]. But Microsoft rode an enterprise cloud cycle; Apple absorbed a post-pandemic hardware normalization. The relevant question for this Tribunal is the current trajectory, and on the current numbers, the two companies are growing at nearly identical rates.

**REBUTTAL TO CHARGE 2: The FY2024 Net Income Dip Was Not Operational — and FY2025 Set a Record.**

Examine the divergence the Prosecution ignores: in FY2024, **operating income rose to a record $123.22B** (operating margin 31.5%, up from 29.8%) while net income fell to $93.74B [Exhibit A]. When the operating engine strengthens but the bottom line dips, the cause sits *below* the operating line — a non-operating, non-recurring item, not business decay. The proof is FY2025: net income of **$112.01B, an all-time record, at a 26.9% net margin** — the highest annual net margin in the five-year record [Exhibit A]. A structural earnings problem does not resolve itself into a record year twelve months later.

**REBUTTAL TO CHARGE 3: The Cash Followed — Look at the Most Recent Data.**

The Prosecution asks why cash doesn't follow earnings. It does. The quarter ending 2025-12-27 produced **$53.92B in operating cash flow, up 80% from $29.93B** in the year-ago quarter [Exhibit A]. That single quarter's cash generation exceeds Microsoft's best quarter on record ($46.68B, Q ending 2026-03-31) [Exhibit B].

The Defense concedes the FY2025 annual figure ($111.48B vs. $118.25B in FY2024) declined, and the record before this court does not explain why. But every one of the last five fiscal years exceeded $104B in operating cash flow [Exhibit A] — this is variance around an enormous base, not erosion, and the freshest quarterly datapoint points sharply upward.

**REBUTTAL TO CHARGE 4: The Prosecution Has Discovered the Holiday Season.**

The "sequential collapse" from the December quarter is the most predictable pattern in Apple's filings. Compare the December quarters year-over-year: the prior year's holiday quarter was followed by the same step-down (Q ending 2025-03-29: $95.36B; Q ending 2025-06-28: $94.04B) [Exhibit A]. The honest comparison is year-over-year, and it demolishes the charge:

- Revenue: **$109.42B vs. $94.04B — +16.4%** [Exhibit A]
- Operating income: **$35.70B vs. $28.20B — up ~27%** [Exhibit A]
- Gross margin: **50.1% — the highest in the entire record**, up from 46.5% a year prior [Exhibit A]

As for the cash "drain" to $39.54B: that figure is *higher* than the $36.27B held one year earlier, and stockholders' equity rose to $107.52B in the same quarter [Exhibit A]. Quarterly cash balances fluctuate at peers as well — Microsoft's cash moved from $30.24B to $20.93B across its fiscal year [Exhibit B]. Point-in-time cash is treasury management, not distress.

**REBUTTAL TO CHARGE 5: The Balance Sheet Was Not Hollowed Out — It Was Deliberately Optimized, and It Has Been Rebuilt.**

The low FY2022 equity reflects capital returned to shareholders, not losses — a company earning ~$100B annually [Exhibit A] does not deplete equity by accident. And the trajectory since is unambiguous:

- Stockholders' equity: **$50.67B (FY2022) → $107.52B (Q ending 2026-06-27)** — more than doubled [Exhibit A]
- Long-term debt: **$109.11B (FY2021) → $71.34B** — cut by roughly a third [Exhibit A]
- LT-debt/equity: **1.95 → 0.66** [Exhibit A]
- Cash: **$23.65B (FY2022) → $39.54B** [Exhibit A]

The Defense concedes Microsoft runs more conservatively (LT-debt/equity of 0.07 [Exhibit B]). But the charge is that Apple is *hollowing out* its balance sheet; every recent datapoint shows the opposite — sustained, simultaneous deleveraging and equity rebuilding.

**REBUTTAL TO CHARGE 6: Interest Is a Rounding Error; R&D Is the Reason for the Record Margins.**

Interest expense of $3.93B in FY2023 sits against operating income of $114.30B — coverage of roughly 29 times [Exhibit A]. And the debt on which that interest is paid has since fallen from $95.28B to $71.34B [Exhibit A]. This is not a cost-of-capital problem.

On R&D: Apple's 58% increase since FY2021 is *smaller* than the industry benchmark — Microsoft grew R&D from $20.72B to $35.56B over the same span, roughly 72% [Exhibit B]. As a share of revenue, Apple's FY2025 R&D ($34.55B on $416.16B, ~8.3%) is *leaner* than Microsoft's ($35.56B on $331.84B, ~10.7%) [Exhibits A, B]. And "diminishing returns"? Gross margin expanded from 41.8% (FY2021) to 46.9% (FY2025) to **50.1% in the latest quarter**; operating margin from 29.8% to 32.6% [Exhibit A]. The R&D is not burning value — it is visibly compounding it.

---

**DEFENSE SUMMATION:** Strip away the Prosecution's selective timeline and seasonality error, and the record shows: revenue growing 16%+ year-over-year in the latest quarters, matching the sector's best performer [Exhibits A, B]; record annual net income and record gross margins; quarterly operating cash flow up 80% year-over-year; debt down a third with equity more than doubled. The Defense concedes a genuine soft patch in FY2023–2024 and an unexplained FY2025 annual cash-flow dip. But this Tribunal is asked to judge the company before it today — and the freshest sworn figures in evidence describe a business accelerating, not deteriorating. The Defense rests.
rebuttal:
# SEC TRIBUNAL — PROSECUTION'S REBUTTAL
## In re: Apple Inc. (AAPL, CIK 0000320193)

Your Honors, the Prosecution will be brief. Counsel for the defense argued several points well — the seasonality objection to Charge 4's sequential framing is fair on this record, as is the deleveraging evidence on Charge 5, and the Prosecution does not press those further. But the defense's case has two soft joints, and it made concessions the record must preserve.

---

**FIRST: The cash-flow defense collapsed under its own concession — and the earnings-quality problem is worse than charged.**

The defense stated, verbatim: *"The Defense concedes the FY2025 annual figure ($111.48B vs. $118.25B in FY2024) declined, and the record before this court does not explain why."* Let the record reflect that concession. Charge 3 stands admitted in substance.

Now examine what the defense's own framing exposes. In FY2022, Apple converted $99.80B of net income into **$122.15B** of operating cash — roughly $1.22 of cash per dollar of earnings [Exhibit A]. In FY2025, the year of "record" net income of $112.01B, operating cash flow was **$111.48B** — cash conversion of essentially 1.00, and an annual cash figure *still below the FY2022 peak three years later*, despite revenue rising $21.8B over the same span [Exhibit A]. Reported earnings hit a record; cash generation did not. That gap is the definition of deteriorating earnings quality, and the defense told this Tribunal it cannot explain it. Its answer — one strong quarter of $53.92B — is a single datapoint offered against an admitted, unexplained full-year decline.

**SECOND: The rebuttal to Charge 2 is not evidence. It is speculation.**

The defense asserts the FY2024 net income decline was caused by "a non-operating, non-recurring item." Your Honors, search Exhibit A: no such item appears anywhere in the record. What the sworn filings actually show is net income falling two consecutive years — $99.80B → $97.00B → **$93.74B** — and FY2024 net margin of **24.0%**, the *lowest in the entire five-year record*, in the very year the defense calls operationally record-setting [Exhibit A]. The decline is documented; the exculpatory explanation is invented. The Tribunal should credit the numbers, not counsel's theory of what might sit below the operating line. The FY2025 recovery is real, but it does not retroactively supply evidence that the FY2024 decline was benign.

**THIRD: The concessions, for the record.**

The defense has formally conceded: (1) that Apple underperformed through FY2023–2024 — "a genuine soft patch," including the **-2.8%** revenue contraction and FY2024 revenue of $391.04B still below FY2022's $394.33B [Exhibit A] — the substance of Charge 1; (2) that FY2025 operating cash flow declined by ~$6.8B and that this decline is *unexplained on the record* — the substance of Charge 3; and (3) that its chosen peer runs a materially more conservative balance sheet.

---

**SUMMATION:** The defense wins on seasonality and on deleveraging; the Prosecution does not pretend otherwise. But it has *admitted* the growth stall, *admitted* the cash-flow decline it cannot explain, and answered a two-year earnings contraction with an explanation found nowhere in evidence. Three charges stand — one of them by the defense's own mouth. The Prosecution rests.

verdict.summary: The prosecution charged Apple with a multi-year growth stall, declining net income, eroding cash flow, sequential quarterly deterioration, a hollowed balance sheet, and rising costs with diminishing R&D returns. The defense demonstrated that the freshest evidence — FY2025 revenue of $416.16B (+6.4%), record net income of $112.01B, 16%+ year-over-year quarterly growth, record 50.1% gross margins, and substantial deleveraging — refutes most charges, while conceding a genuine FY2023–2024 soft patch and an unexplained FY2025 operating cash flow decline. The Tribunal dismisses three charges outright, sustains the cash-flow charge on the defense's own concession, and finds two charges partially valid as historically accurate but substantially remediated.

verdict.recommendation: The Tribunal finds Apple to be a fundamentally healthy enterprise whose freshest sworn figures — record annual net income, 16%+ year-over-year quarterly revenue growth, record gross margins, and a deliberately deleveraged and rebuilt balance sheet — outweigh a conceded and now-reversed FY2023–2024 growth stall. Investors should note two unresolved blemishes preserved on the record: an admitted, unexplained ~$6.8B decline in FY2025 operating cash flow alongside record earnings (a cash-conversion question worth monitoring in coming filings), and the absence of documented evidence explaining the FY2024 net income dip. On balance, the evidence describes a business accelerating rather than deteriorating; the company merits a favorable assessment, with investors advised to watch whether annual cash generation reconverges with reported earnings.
